name: souffle
why: Datalog logic language for static analysis, an unusual declarative paradigm worth a look.

brief.what_it_is: Soufflé is a language and tool for static analysis, described as similar to Datalog but with records (terms that act like tuples or ADTs). You write analysis rules declaratively as logic, and the tool compiles them into parallel C++ or runs them through an interpreter. The README also mentions an extended I/O system for relations, including SQLite3 interfaces, plus C++ and SWIG interfaces for embedding. The scout data lists three executables: souffle, souffle-compile.py, and souffleprof. The README itself does not describe their inputs and outputs in detail.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a way to rapid-prototype analysis problems with logic, enabling deep design-space exploration while still scaling to large programs such as points-to analysis for Java, taint analysis, and security checks. It presents Datalog-style logic as a domain-specific language for analysis problems.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage describes Futamura projections and partial evaluation as the basis for translating programs into parallel C++, with optimized staged compilation and specialized data structures for logical relations. The README adds that Soufflé uses de-specialization techniques for efficient interpretation and optimal index selection for its relation data structures.

commands_seen.context: Shown with a $ prompt in the README. It clones the source repository, which is the route the README gives for building from source instead of using a packaged release.

brief.install_notes: The README says that on Ubuntu, Fedora, or Oracle Linux you can get a packaged version from the GitHub Releases section. Otherwise you clone the source and follow the build instructions at souffle-lang.github.io/build, which I did not fetch. The README also points to a developer tutorial at souffle-lang.github.io/development for building and developing. The README does not mention macOS or Homebrew. The brew formula is what the scout data relied on, and I did not verify it.
brief.standout: Soufflé compiles Datalog-style analysis programs to parallel C++ and also interprets them, which is less common than pure interpreters or engines. Its homepage pitches the compile step through partial evaluation, and the README cites provenance/debugging and profiling tools as built-in features.
brief.status: unknown. Neither page showed a release date, last-commit date, or maintenance note. The README does show active-looking CI badges, a Releases section, and a discussions board, but that is not proof of current activity.
brief.caveats: The README says the language extends classic Datalog, for example with unbounded recursion over numbers and terms, so it is not strictly pure Datalog. Code written for older versions may need the --legacy command-line flag or a legacy pragma in the source. I did not read the build page, so build complexity is unverified. The README says Soufflé uses clang-format and clang-tidy in CI. The license is UPL-1.0, per the README badge.
quotes: Rapid-prototyping for your analysis problems with logic; enabling deep design-space explorations; designed for large-scale static analysis; e.g., points-to analysis for Java, taint-analysis, security checks.

judge.reason: Soufflé turns declarative Datalog analyses into parallel C++, making a powerful logic-programming paradigm practical for large-scale program analysis.

entry.title: Soufflé
entry.tldr: Soufflé is a Datalog-style logic language that compiles analysis rules into parallel C++, built for questions like points-to and taint analysis over large programs.
entry.deeper_look:
Soufflé is a language and tool for static analysis. You write rules as logic: facts go in, relations are derived from them, and the tool works out how to compute the answer. The README describes the language as "similar to Datalog (but has terms known as records)", and says it is frequently used as a domain-specific language for analysis problems.

The tool can run a program through an interpreter or compile it into parallel C++. The homepage credits Futamura projections and partial evaluation for the compile step, with specialized data structures for relations. The README adds de-specialization for efficient interpretation and optimal index selection. It also lists an extended I/O system for relations, including SQLite3 interfaces, plus C++ and SWIG interfaces for embedding. Provenance, debugging and profiling tools are described as built in.

The idea underneath is that many analysis problems, such as which pointers can reach which objects or where tainted data can flow, are recursive queries over relations. If you state the rules and leave out the evaluation strategy, you can try design variations quickly. The README pitches it as "rapid-prototyping for your analysis problems with logic", yet it is meant to scale to large programs, such as Java points-to analysis.

The language extends classic Datalog, for example with unbounded recursion over numbers and terms, so it is not pure Datalog.
entry.install:
brew install souffle
# The README does not mention macOS or Homebrew; it points to packaged releases for Ubuntu, Fedora and Oracle Linux, or a source build (git clone https://github.com/souffle-lang/souffle.git, then follow souffle-lang.github.io/build).

entry.whats_unique: Soufflé both interprets Datalog-style programs and compiles them to parallel C++ through partial evaluation, rather than being only an interpreter or a query engine.
